approved: Moved the bill to establish a Commonwealth public interest disclosure scheme that facilitates reporting and investigation of suspected wrongdoing, protects officials from liability and reprisals, permits limited public disclosure, and gives oversight roles to the Ombudsman and the Inspector-General of Intelligence and Security.

Said the coalition would not oppose the Public Interest Disclosure Bill but criticised Labor for taking until the final days of parliament to deliver on a 2007 election promise, noting a parliamentary committee reported on the issue in January 2009 and the government did not respond until March 2010.

Supported the Public Interest Disclosure Bill 2013, Australia's first stand-alone federal whistleblower protection scheme, praising Attorney-General Mark Dreyfus for chairing the 2008 parliamentary inquiry that led to it, and said the legislation supports Australia's compliance with the United Nations Convention against Corruption.

Supported the Public Interest Disclosure Bill, quoting a Parliamentary Library research paper noting the Commonwealth was the only Australian jurisdiction without dedicated legislation protecting whistleblowers, after a series of earlier private members' bills had lapsed for lack of government support.

Supported the Public Interest Disclosure Bill, tracing whistleblower protection efforts back to a 1994 Senate committee report, and noted that three earlier private members' bills on the issue, introduced by Senator Andrew Murray, all lapsed without coalition government support.

Summed up the second reading debate on the Public Interest Disclosure Bill, noting House and Senate committees had together received more than 30 submissions and both recommended the bill pass, and confirmed the scheme covers intelligence agencies internally while excluding members of parliament, their staff and federal judicial officers from its protections.

Moved amendments to the Public Interest Disclosure (Consequential Amendments) Bill 2013 concerning the Ombudsman's investigative powers and the wording of an agency's conduct and actions, referring to an earlier contribution and commending the amendments to the House.

The government introduced the Public Interest Disclosure Bill 2013 to create the first stand‑alone federal whistleblower protection scheme, enabling Commonwealth public officials to report suspected wrongdoing and receive protections against reprisal. The bill also established oversight roles for the Commonwealth Ombudsman and the Inspector‑General of Intelligence and Security, and a companion bill repealed existing whistleblower provisions in the Public Service Act 1999 and Parliamentary Service Act 1999.

The Greens senator argued that the Public Interest Disclosure Bill 2013 is overly complex but supported it, announcing a secured amendment allowing whistleblowers to immediately disclose imminent environmental threats. He called for a national anticorruption commission and criticised the Australian Federal Police's treatment of whistleblowers, citing the cases of Allan Kessing, Ross Fusca and Brendan Thomson.
